title: In the Name of the Law
paragraphs: A police true-crime dramatization based on actual case files, reconstructing investigations of crimes ranging from theft to murder.
1936 syndicated police-case anthology claiming to dramatize actual crime files.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1936 syndicated run (1936 to 1936).
Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Ken Christy (performer).
The stories often return to true crime and police case files, police investigation and detection, 1930s syndicated radio, homicide investigation, prison escape and manhunt, and narcotics smuggling.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Fragmentary and disputed collector chronology and 1930s syndicated true-crime police anthology.

A police true-crime dramatization based on actual case files, reconstructing investigations of crimes ranging from theft to murder.

1936 syndicated police-case anthology claiming to dramatize actual crime files.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1936 syndicated run (1936 to 1936).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Ken Christy (performer).

The stories often return to true crime and police case files, police investigation and detection, 1930s syndicated radio, homicide investigation, prison escape and manhunt, and narcotics smuggling.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Fragmentary and disputed collector chronology and 1930s syndicated true-crime police anthology.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include A Man Called X, Academy Award Theater, Barrie Craig, Calling All Cars, and Dr. Kildare.
